payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the eternal Way; the Name that can be named is not the eternal Name; the Nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; the Name is the mother of all things. The eternal Way is without desire to contemplate its subtlety; the eternal Name is with desire to contemplate its limits. These two are of the same origin but different names; they are called the "Mysterious." The Mysterious is the Mysterious again and again; the Gate of the Many Subtleties.

issues.span: The eternal Way is without desire to contemplate its subtlety; the eternal Name is with desire to contemplate its limits.
issues.advice: The source reads 常無欲以觀其妙，常有欲以觀其徼 — the subject is the person who constantly has no desires / constantly has desires, not 'the eternal Way/Name'. Render as something like 'Always without desire, one contemplates its subtlety; always with desire, one contemplates its limits.'

issues.span: the Name is the mother of all things
issues.advice: Source has 有名萬物之母 — 'the named' (having names) is the mother of the ten thousand things, parallel to 無名. 'the Name' shifts the sense; use 'the named' or 'what has a name'.

issues.span: the Nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth
issues.advice: Acceptable, but ensure parallelism with the corrected 'the named' clause; 無名/有名 are 'the nameless'/'the named', not 'the Name'.

issues.span: the Gate of the Many Subtleties
issues.advice: 衆妙之門 is conventionally 'the gate of all wonders/marvels'; 'Many Subtleties' is nonstandard and awkward. Use 'the gate of all wonders'.

issues.span: The Mysterious is the Mysterious again and again; the Gate of the Many Subtleties.
issues.advice: The final clause lacks a verb and reads as a fragment; render 玄之又玄，衆妙之門 as 'Mystery upon mystery — the gate of all wonders.'

payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the eternal Way; the Name that can be named is not the eternal Name; the nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; the named is the mother of all things. Always without desire, one contemplates its subtlety; always with desire, one contemplates its limits. These two are of the same origin but different names; they are called the "Mystery upon mystery." Mystery upon mystery is the gate of all wonders.

issues.span: they are called the "Mystery upon mystery." Mystery upon mystery is the gate of all wonders.
issues.advice: The quoted phrase 'Mystery upon mystery' is awkwardly placed as a name for the pair; consider rendering 同謂之玄 as 'both are called the Mystery' and 玄之又玄 as 'Mystery within mystery' or 'the deepest mystery' to preserve the distinction between the two clauses.

payload.translation: Le savoir peut être dit, mais il n'est pas le même; le nom peut être nommé, mais il n'est pas le même. Le nom sans nom est le commencement du ciel et de la terre; le nom est la mère des choses. Le vide constant est désiré pour observer la sagesse; le désir constant est désiré pour observer les limites. Ces deux sont d'un même origine mais d'un nom différent; on les appelle ensemble le Mystère. Le Mystère est le Mystère, et le Mystère est le Mystère; la porte des choses infinies.

issues.span: Le savoir peut être dit, mais il n'est pas le même
issues.advice: The source 道可道非常道 means 'the Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way'; 道 is rendered as 'savoir' (knowledge), which is a mistranslation. Use 'la Voie' and 'constant/éternel' rather than 'le même'.

issues.span: le nom peut être nommé, mais il n'est pas le même
issues.advice: Should be 'le nom qui peut être nommé n'est pas le nom constant' — 'pas le même' mistranslates 非常名.

issues.span: Le nom sans nom est le commencement du ciel et de la terre
issues.advice: Source 無名天地之始 means 'the nameless is the origin of heaven and earth'; 'le nom sans nom' adds 'nom' incorrectly. Render as 'l'innommé' or 'le sans-nom'.

issues.span: le nom est la mère des choses
issues.advice: Source 有名萬物之母 means 'the named is the mother of the ten thousand things'; 'le nom' loses 有 (the named). Use 'le nommé'.

issues.span: Le vide constant est désiré pour observer la sagesse
issues.advice: Source 常無欲以觀其妙 means 'constantly without desire, one observes its mystery/wonder'; the translation inverts it into 'le vide constant est désiré' and renders 妙 as 'sagesse'. Should be 'sans désir constant, on observe sa merveille'.

issues.span: le désir constant est désiré pour observer les limites
issues.advice: Source 常有欲以觀其徼 means 'constantly having desire, one observes its manifestations/boundaries'; 'le désir constant est désiré' is a mistranslation. Use 'avec désir, on observe ses manifestations'.

issues.span: Le Mystère est le Mystère, et le Mystère est le Mystère
issues.advice: Source 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery' / 'plus mystérieux que le mystère'; the repetition is a mistranslation, not a rendering of 又.

issues.span: la porte des choses infinies
issues.advice: Source 衆妙之門 means 'the gate of all wonders/marvels'; 'choses infinies' mistranslates 衆妙.

issues.span: le Mystère
issues.advice: 玄 is conventionally rendered 'le Mystère' or 'l'obscur'; acceptable, but consistency with 妙 (merveille) should be maintained.

issues.span: Ces deux sont d'un même origine mais d'un nom différent
issues.advice: Grammatically should be 'd'une même origine' (feminine).

issues.span: Le savoir
issues.advice: Rendering 道 as 'savoir' misrepresents the Daoist concept; use 'la Voie' to preserve cultural meaning.

payload.translation: La Voie que l'on peut dire n'est pas la Voie qui est éternelle ; le nom qui peut être nommé n'est pas le nom qui est éternel. L'innommé est le commencement du ciel et de la terre ; le nommé est la mère des choses. Le vide constant est observé sans désir pour observer sa merveille ; avec désir constant, on observe ses manifestations. Ces deux sont d'une même origine mais d'un nom différent ; on les appelle ensemble le Mystère. Le Mystère est le Mystère, et le Mystère est le Mystère ; la porte des choses infinies.

issues.span: Le vide constant est observé sans désir pour observer sa merveille
issues.advice: The source 常無欲以觀其妙 means 'constantly without desire, in order to observe its subtlety/wonder'; the translation introduces 'le vide constant' (constant emptiness) which is not in the source and misassigns the subject. Render as 'Toujours sans désir, on observe sa merveille'.

issues.span: avec désir constant, on observe ses manifestations
issues.advice: Source 常有欲以觀其徼 means 'constantly having desire, in order to observe its manifestations/boundaries'; 'désir constant' slightly shifts the adverb from the verb to the noun. Prefer 'ayant toujours du désir, on observe ses manifestations'.

issues.span: Le Mystère est le Mystère, et le Mystère est le Mystère
issues.advice: Source 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery' / 'plus mystérieux encore', not a tautological repetition. Render as 'Mystère des mystères' or 'mystérieux encore et toujours'.

issues.span: Le Mystère est le Mystère, et le Mystère est le Mystère ; la porte des choses infinies.
issues.advice: The tautology is awkward and the final clause lacks a verb; restructure as '...; c'est la porte de toutes les merveilles.'

issues.span: la porte des choses infinies
issues.advice: Source 衆妙之門 is 'the gate of all subtleties/wonders' (衆妙), not 'choses infinies'. Use 'la porte de toutes les merveilles'.

issues.span: le nom qui est éternel
issues.advice: Source 常名 is 'the constant/unchanging name'; 'éternel' is acceptable but 'constant' better mirrors 常 used consistently. Consider 'le nom constant'.

payload.translation: La Voie que l'on peut dire n'est pas la Voie qui est constante ; le nom constant n'est pas le nom qui est éternel. L'inconnu est le commencement du ciel et de la terre ; le connu est la mère des choses. Toujours sans désir, on observe sa merveille ; ayant toujours du désir, on observe ses manifestations. Ces deux sont d'une même origine mais d'un nom différent ; on les appelle ensemble le Mystère des mystères. Le Mystère est le Mystère ; le Mystère est le Mystère ; c'est la porte de toutes les merveilles.

issues.span: le nom constant n'est pas le nom qui est éternel
issues.advice: The source 名可名非常名 means 'the name that can be named is not the constant name'; the translation inverts the structure and adds 'éternel' not present in the source.

issues.span: L'inconnu est le commencement du ciel et de la terre ; le connu est la mère des choses
issues.advice: 無名/有名 means 'the nameless' and 'the named', not 'l'inconnu/le connu' (the unknown/the known); this changes the meaning.

issues.span: Le Mystère est le Mystère ; le Mystère est le Mystère
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery' / 'mystère au-delà du mystère'; the repeated tautology is a mistranslation and omits 同謂之玄's referent.

issues.span: la Voie qui est constante
issues.advice: 常道 is conventionally rendered 'la Voie constante' / 'la Voie éternelle'; the relative clause plus 'constante' is inconsistent with the standard Daoist term.

issues.span: Ces deux sont d'une même origine mais d'un nom différent ; on les appelle ensemble le Mystère des mystères
issues.advice: 同出而異名 means 'same origin but different names'; 'd'un nom différent' is ungrammatical/awkward French and the sentence structure is garbled.

payload.translation: 道は言及せず、道は常なり。名は言及せず、名は常なり。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母なり。常無を欲せずにして妙を観ず。常有を欲せずにして徼を観ず。この二者は同一の源から出ているが異名を有する。これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門なり。

issues.span: 道は言及せず、道は常なり。名は言及せず、名は常なり。
issues.advice: The source says '道可道非常道' = the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the translation inverts the meaning, asserting the Dao is not spoken and is constant. Render the conditional/negation correctly.

issues.span: 常無を欲せずにして妙を観ず。常有を欲せずにして徼を観ず。
issues.advice: Source means '常に無欲にして以て其の妙を観、常に有欲にして以て其の徼を観' — constantly without desire to observe the mystery, constantly with desire to observe the manifestations. The translation negates 欲 in both clauses, reversing the meaning.

issues.span: 無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母なり。
issues.advice: Source is '無名天地之始、有名萬物之母' — acceptable in meaning but should preserve the parallel structure; the rendering is roughly adequate here.

issues.span: 道は言及せず
issues.advice: '可道' is not 'mentioning'; it means 'can be spoken/expressed as the Dao'. Use a rendering like '道として言い表せる道は'.

issues.span: 玄之又玄
issues.advice: This is a classical phrase meaning 'mystery upon mystery'; leaving it as an unglossed fragment breaks the sentence. Render as '玄の又玄' with a connective so the clause reads grammatically.

issues.span: これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門なり。
issues.advice: The sentence is broken: '玄之又玄' is left dangling and '衆妙の門なり' lacks a subject/connection. Join as 'これを玄と謂う。玄の又玄、衆妙の門なり。'

payload.translation: 道として言い表せる道は、常なり。名として言い表せる名は、常なり。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母なり。常に無欲にして以て其の妙を観ず。常に有欲にして以て其の徼を観ず。この二者は同一の源から出ているが異名を有する。これを玄と呼び、玄の又玄。衆妙の門なり。

issues.span: 道として言い表せる道は、常なり。名として言い表せる名は、常なり。
issues.advice: The source says 非常道 / 非常名 ('is not the constant Dao/name'). The translation asserts the opposite ('is constant'). Render the negation: e.g. 常の道にあらず / 常の名にあらず.

issues.span: 常に無欲にして以て其の妙を観ず。常に有欲にして以て其の徼を観ず。
issues.advice: The source 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 is a conditional/parallel construction ('always without desire, in order to observe its wonder; always with desire, in order to observe its boundary'). The translation reads as flat assertions; preserve the 以て purpose relation and the contrast between 無欲/有欲.

issues.span: 此兩者同出而異名同謂之玄
issues.advice: The source says the two emerge together and are 'the same, called 玄' (同謂之玄). The translation says '同一の源から出ているが異名を有する。これを玄と呼び' — acceptable in gist but should keep 同謂之玄 ('both are called the mysterious') rather than only 'this is called X'.

issues.span: 徼
issues.advice: 徼 (jiào) means 'boundary/manifestation/outcome'; rendering as 徼 untranslated or as 'boundary' should be consistent. Ensure a standard gloss (e.g. 端境・顕現) rather than leaving ambiguous.

issues.span: 玄の又玄
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 is 'mystery upon mystery'; the Japanese should read 玄の又玄 or 玄にして又玄 — the current phrasing is awkward and loses the reduplicative rhetorical force.

payload.translation: 道は常なり。名は常なり。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母なり。常に無欲にして以て其の妙を観ず。常に有欲にして以て其の徼を観ず。此二者は同一の源から出り、異名を有する。これを玄と呼び、玄の又玄なり。衆妙の門なり。

issues.span: 道は常なり。名は常なり。
issues.advice: The source says 道可道非常道名可名非常名 — 'the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the name that can be named is not the constant name.' The translation omits the conditional/negation entirely and asserts 'the Dao is constant, the name is constant,' which inverts the meaning. Render the full clause including 可道/可名 and 非常.

issues.span: 此二者は同一の源から出り
issues.advice: Source 同出 means 'emerge together (from the same source)' — acceptable, but the preceding clauses 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 are rendered as separate assertions without the 欲 ('desire') nuance; ensure 無欲/有欲 are preserved as 'without desire / with desire' rather than dropped.

issues.span: 玄の又玄なり
issues.advice: Source 玄之又玄 is 'mystery upon mystery' (deepening), not 'the mystery of mystery' as a static equation; render the reduplicative 又 as 'upon/again'.

issues.span: 徼
issues.advice: 徼 (jiào) means 'the outer manifestation/boundary/appearance' contrasted with 妙 'subtlety'; the translation leaves it untranslated as 徼, which is not a Japanese term. Render as 端緒/顕現/境界 etc.

issues.span: 出り
issues.advice: '出り' is not standard Japanese; use 出でたり or 生ず.

payload.translation: The highest virtue is like water: it benefits all things without striving. It dwells where others find no place; it is deep and humble; it is kind and compassionate; it speaks truthfully; it governs affairs wisely; it is capable of action at the right time. For it is because it does not strive.

issues.span: it is deep and humble; it is kind and compassionate
issues.advice: The source lists parallel phrases 居善地/心善淵/與善仁/言善信/政善治/事善能/動善時, each with a distinct subject (dwelling, heart/mind, association, speech, governance, affairs, movement). The translation collapses 心善淵 and 與善仁 into vague adjectives and drops the parallel structure; render each clause with its own subject (e.g., 'in its heart it loves depth; in association it is benevolent').

issues.span: it governs affairs wisely
issues.advice: 政善治 refers to governance/rule being well-ordered, not 'governs affairs'; and 事善能 ('in affairs it is capable') is a separate clause that is missing. Restore both distinct clauses.

issues.span: For it is because it does not strive.
issues.advice: The source ends with 夫惟不爭 (only because it does not strive), a causal conclusion tied to 故幾於道 earlier; the translation is a dangling fragment. Complete the causal clause (e.g., 'It is only because it does not strive [that it is without fault / near to the Way]').

issues.span: It dwells where others find no place
issues.advice: 處衆人之所惡 means it dwells in places people despise/dislike, not 'where others find no place'; adjust to 'dwells in what others disdain'.

issues.span: it is capable of action at the right time
issues.advice: 動善時 means 'in movement/action it is timely'; the translation merges 事善能 and 動善時 and omits 事善能. Separate the two clauses.

payload.translation: The highest virtue is like water: it benefits all things without striving. It dwells in places where others find no place; it is deep and humble; it is kind and compassionate; it speaks truthfully; it governs affairs wisely; it is capable of action at the right time. It is only because it does not strive that it is without fault and near to the Way.

issues.span: It dwells in places where others find no place
issues.advice: The source 處衆人之所惡 means 'dwells in places that others despise/dislike', not 'where others find no place'. Render as 'dwells in places others despise'.

issues.span: it is deep and humble
issues.advice: 心善淵 means 'its heart is good at being deep/profound' — the 'humble' addition is not in the source; keep 'its heart is deep'.

issues.span: it is kind and compassionate
issues.advice: 與善仁 means 'in association it is good at being benevolent/kind'; 'compassionate' is an added nuance not present. Use 'in its relations it is benevolent'.

issues.span: it governs affairs wisely
issues.advice: 政善治 means 'in governing it is good at ordering/managing'; 'wisely' is an addition. Use 'in governing it is good at ordering'.

issues.span: it is capable of action at the right time
issues.advice: 事善能動善時 are two clauses: 'in affairs it is good at being capable; in action it is good at timing'. The translation merges them and drops 事善能.

issues.span: it is without fault and near to the Way
issues.advice: 故幾於道 means 'therefore it is close to the Way'; 'without fault' (無尤) belongs to the final 夫惟不爭 clause and is misplaced here. Keep 'therefore it is near to the Way' and attach 'without fault' to the non-striving clause.

issues.span: It is only because it does not strive that it is without fault and near to the Way
issues.advice: The source ends 夫惟不爭 (only because it does not strive) — 'without fault' (無尤) is not in this text; remove 'without fault' or note it is absent from source.

payload.translation: The highest virtue is like water: it benefits all things without striving. It dwells in places others despise. It is deep and humble; it is kind and benevolent; it speaks truthfully; it governs affairs wisely; it is capable of action at the right time. It is only because it does not strive that it is near to the Way.

issues.span: It is only because it does not strive that it is near to the Way.
issues.advice: The source's 故幾於道 ('therefore it is close to the Way') is a consequence of 處衆人之所惡 (dwelling where others despise), not of 不爭. The causal link is misplaced; 夫惟不爭 is the concluding clause, not the cause of 幾於道.

issues.span: It is deep and humble; it is kind and benevolent; it speaks truthfully; it governs affairs wisely; it is capable of action at the right time.
issues.advice: The seven parallel phrases 居善地/心善淵/與善仁/言善信/政善治/事善能/動善時 are each 'X is good at/apt in Y'. The rendering collapses 居善地 (dwelling in good ground) into the preceding sentence and merges 心善淵 with 'humble', losing the distinct 居/心/與/言/政/事/動 subjects.

issues.span: It dwells in places others despise.
issues.advice: This is a separate clause (處衆人之所惡) and should be kept distinct from 居善地, which is omitted or conflated.

payload.translation: Le plus haut bien est comme l'eau : l'eau profite à tout le monde sans se battre. Elle habite là où les autres s'abstiennent, car elle est proche du Dao. Elle habite le lieu bien choisi, le fond profond, la bonté, la parole de foi, le gouvernement, l'administration, l'action, et le temps. C'est parce qu'elle ne se bat pas.

issues.span: Elle habite là où les autres s'abstiennent
issues.advice: The source says 處衆人之所惡 'dwells in places that people despise/dislike'; 's'abstiennent' (abstain) misrepresents 惡 (loathe/dislike). Render as 'elle demeure là où les gens répugnent' or similar.

issues.span: Elle habite le lieu bien choisi, le fond profond, la bonté, la parole de foi, le gouvernement, l'administration, l'action, et le temps
issues.advice: The seven 善 phrases (居善地, 心善淵, 與善仁, 言善信, 政善治, 事善能, 動善時) describe the sage's qualities, not the water 'habiting' each. The translation collapses them into a list attached to 'elle habite', losing 心善淵 (heart/mind), 與善仁 (in giving/association), and mistranslating 政善治 and 動善時. Restructure as separate clauses about the person: 'sa demeure est bien située, son cœur est profond, dans ses dons il est bien

issues.span: C'est parce qu'elle ne se bat pas.
issues.advice: The source ends 夫惟不爭 (only because he/it does not contend) — an incomplete clause leading into the next chapter; the translation adds a period and 'C'est parce que', which is acceptable but the sentence is left dangling. Consider 'C'est justement parce qu'il ne rivalise pas...' to preserve the open-ended structure.

issues.span: sans se battre
issues.advice: 不爭 is a key Daoist term meaning 'not contending/rivaling'; 'se battre' (to fight) is too physical. Prefer 'sans rivaliser' or 'sans contester'.

issues.span: le gouvernement, l'administration
issues.advice: 政善治 is one phrase ('in governing, he governs well'); splitting into 'gouvernement, administration' as two list items is awkward and redundant.

payload.translation: Le plus haut bien est comme l'eau : l'eau profite à tout le monde sans rivaliser. Elle demeure là où les gens répugnent, car elle est proche du Dao. Sa demeure est bien située, son cœur est profond, dans ses dons il est bienveillant, dans sa parole il est fidèle, dans son gouvernement il est sage, dans ses actions il est habile, et dans son temps il est opportun. C'est justement parce qu'il ne rivalise pas.

issues.span: C'est justement parce qu'il ne rivalise pas.
issues.advice: The source ends with 夫惟不爭 ('only because he does not contend'), which in the Laozi continues '故無尤' (therefore he has no fault). The translation leaves the final clause incomplete and dangling; either render the full sense or note the truncated source, but the sentence as given is grammatically incomplete in French.

issues.span: Elle demeure là où les gens répugnent, car elle est proche du Dao.
issues.advice: The causal 'car' is not in the source; 故幾於道 means 'therefore it is close to the Dao', following from dwelling in lowly places, not a reason for dwelling there. Recast to preserve the consequential relation.

issues.span: dans ses dons il est bienveillant
issues.advice: The subject shifts awkwardly between 'elle' (l'eau) and 'il' (the sage/善者). Keep a consistent subject or make the shift explicit for readability.

payload.translation: Le plus haut bien est comme l'eau : l'eau profite à tout le monde sans rivaliser. Elle demeure là où les gens répugnent, car elle est proche du Dao. Sa demeure est bien placée, son cœur est profond, dans ses dons il est bienveillant, dans sa parole il est fidèle, dans son gouvernement il est sage, dans ses actions il est habile, et dans son temps il est opportun. C'est précisément parce qu'il ne rivalise pas.

issues.span: C'est précisément parce qu'il ne rivalise pas.
issues.advice: The source ends with 夫惟不爭, which is an incomplete clause introducing a consequence (故無尤 in the received text). The translation leaves the sentence dangling; either render the full clause or mark the ellipsis so the reader knows the thought is unfinished.

issues.span: Elle demeure là où les gens répugnent, car elle est proche du Dao.
issues.advice: The causal link 'car' is not in the source: 故幾於道 follows 處衆人之所惡 as a consequence of the water's conduct, not as a reason for dwelling there. Recast so that 'being close to the Dao' is the result, not the cause.

issues.span: dans ses dons il est bienveillant
issues.advice: 與善仁 refers to association/interaction (與 = 'in relations'), not 'dons' (gifts). Translate as 'dans ses relations il est bienveillant' or similar.

issues.span: dans son gouvernement il est sage
issues.advice: 政善治: 治 means 'governs well / brings order', not 'is wise'. Use 'dans son gouvernement il sait gouverner' or 'il ordonne bien'.

issues.span: son cœur est profond
issues.advice: 心善淵 is acceptable but the parallel structure (居/心/與/言/政/事/動 + 善 + noun) is better preserved with a consistent formula; the current mix of 'est bien placée / est profond / est bienveillant' is uneven.

payload.translation: 善行如水，潤澤萬物而不與爭。處群衆之所厭惡，故幾近於道。居善地，心善淵，與善仁，言善信，政善治，事善能動，時善也。夫惟不爭

issues.span: 事善能動，時善也
issues.advice: The source lists seven parallel phrases: 居善地、心善淵、與善仁、言善信、政善治、事善能、動善時. The translation merges 動 into 事善能 and misplaces 時, producing '事善能動，時善也' instead of '事善能，動善時'.

issues.span: 善行如水
issues.advice: 上善 means 'the highest good' (最上の善), not 'good deeds' (善行). Render as '最上の善は水の如し' or equivalent.

issues.span: 潤澤萬物而不與爭
issues.advice: The object of 爭 is missing; the source says 不爭 (does not contend), not 不與爭. Remove 與 or supply the correct object.

issues.span: 處群衆之所厭惡
issues.advice: 衆人 means 'the common people/multitude', not 群衆 in the modern sense; and 所惡 is 'what they dislike'. Rephrase for natural classical register.

payload.translation: 最上の善は水の如し。水は万物を潤澤するが争わず、群衆の嫌う所を居する。故に幾よその道に近し。善地に居し、心は淵、仁は善、信は善、政は治、事は能、動は時。夫惟不爭

issues.span: 故に幾よその道に近し
issues.advice: 「幾」は「ほとんど」の意。原文「故幾於道」は「ゆえに道に近い」であり、「幾よ」という命令・呼びかけの表現は誤り。副詞的に訳すべき。

issues.span: 心は淵、仁は善、信は善、政は治、事は能、動は時
issues.advice: 原文は「居善地、心善淵、與善仁、言善信、政善治、事善能、動善時」で各句「善」を伴う並列。訳文は「善」の対応が不統一で、特に「與善仁」を「仁は善」としている点が原文の構造（與＝交わり）を反映していない。各句の述語構造を揃えて訳すべき。

issues.span: 仁は善
issues.advice: 「與善仁」は「交わりは仁に善し（人と交わるのに仁にかなっている）」の意。「仁は善」では主客が逆転し意味が変わる。

issues.span: 潤澤する
issues.advice: 「利」は「利益を与える・役立てる」の意。「潤澤する」はやや限定的で、万物を「利する」の含意を十分に伝えない。より一般的な「益する」「恵む」等が適切。

issues.span: 夫惟不爭
issues.advice: 原文末尾「夫惟不爭」は前文を受ける結語。「夫れ惟だ争わざるのみ」のように訓読調で補い、文として完結させるべき。

payload.translation: 最上の善は水のように、万物を益する而不争で、群衆の嫌う所を住む。ゆえに道に近い。善地に住み、心は淵、交わりは仁、言は信、政は治、事は能、動は時。夫れ惟は争わざるのみ。

issues.span: 万物を益する而不争で
issues.advice: 「而不争」は漢文の接続表現がそのまま残っており、日本語として意味が通らない。「争わず」と訳すべき。

issues.span: 群衆の嫌う所を住む
issues.advice: 「處衆人之所惡」は「衆人の嫌う所に身を置く」の意。「住む」は「處」の訳として不適切で、「居る」「身を置く」とすべき。

issues.span: 心は淵
issues.advice: 「心善淵」は「心は淵のごとく深し」の意で、単に「淵」とするだけでは意味が不足。

issues.span: 與善仁
issues.advice: 「與」は「交わり」で訳されているが、「與善仁」全体で「交わりは仁」とするのは原文の構造を反映しておらず、「人と交わるに仁」などとすべき。

issues.span: 夫れ惟は争わざるのみ
issues.advice: 「夫惟不爭」は「それ惟だ争わざるのみ」の形で、助詞「は」が不自然。文語調を整えるべき。

issues.span: 善地に住み
issues.advice: 「居善地」の「居」は「住む」より「居る」「身を置く」が適切で、他の「善」の並列構造も統一すべき。

issues.span: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず
issues.advice: The source 持而盈之不如其已 means 'to hold and overfill it is not as good as stopping'; the translation reverses the meaning (止むを得ず = 'cannot help it'). Render as '持して之を盈たすは其の已むに如かず'.

issues.span: 揣て鋭くは長きものなり
issues.advice: Source 揣而銳之不可長保 means 'hammered sharp, it cannot be preserved long'; translation says 'is a long thing', losing the negation. Render as '揣りて之を鋭くするは長く保つべからず'.

issues.span: 金玉は堂に満ちて守り得ず
issues.advice: Source 金玉滿堂莫之能守 means 'gold and jade fill the hall, none can keep them'; translation reads as 'cannot be kept' without the 'no one can' sense and misparses 莫之能守. Render as '金玉堂に満つるも之を守る能うもの莫し'.

issues.span: 富貴は誇りしむと自ら咎を遺すなり
issues.advice: Source 富貴而驕自遺其咎 means 'wealth and honor with arrogance bring self-inflicted blame'; translation's 誇りしむ is unclear and the causal link is weak. Render as '富貴にして驕れば自ら其の咎を遺す'.

issues.span: 功は成り、名は遂ぎて身は退く
issues.advice: Source 功成名遂身退 is a conditional/sequential statement 'when work is done and name achieved, withdraw the self'; the translation presents it as flat description. Render as '功成り名遂げて身退くは'.

issues.advice: 揣 is read はかりて/うがちて in this context (to hammer/beat thin), not 揣て with unclear reading; use '揣りて' or '鎚ちて' with proper okurigana.

issues.span: 長きものなり
issues.advice: This phrasing is unnatural and semantically wrong for 不可長保; use '長く保つべからず'.

payload.translation: 持ちて之を盈たすは其の已むに如かず。揣りて之を鋭くするは長く保つべからず。金玉堂に満つるも之を守る能うもの莫し。富貴にして驕れば自ら其の咎を遺す。功成り名遂げて身退くは。天の道なり。

issues.span: 身退くは。天の道なり。
issues.advice: The period after 退くは is misplaced; it should read 身退くは天の道なり without a break, since は introduces the predicate 天の道なり.

payload.translation: The wise in the past, who mastered the art of being a scholar, were subtle, mysterious, profound, and beyond recognition. For it is precisely because they are unrecognizable that they are strengthened and their demeanor is calm and easy. Like a person wading through a river in winter, they seem to fear their four neighbors; like a guest, they are open and transparent. Like ice, they are clear and unobtrusive, yet they are still. Like a primitive state, they are vast and open. Like a valley, they are full and undifferentiated. What can make them turbid and still? What can make them clear and calm? What can make them tranquil and enduring? The one who seeks to preserve this way does not wish to be full. For it is precisely because they are not full that they can endure without change.

issues.span: who mastered the art of being a scholar
issues.advice: 善為士 means 'skilled in being a true practitioner/master', not 'mastering the art of being a scholar'; the sense of 士 here is a person of the Way, not a scholar.

issues.span: they are strengthened and their demeanor is calm and easy
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'one is forced to describe their appearance/demeanor'; it does not mean 'strengthened'. The clause should convey reluctant description, not strengthening.

issues.span: like a guest, they are open and transparent
issues.advice: 儼若客 means 'solemn/reverent as a guest'; 渙若冰將釋 ('yielding like ice about to melt') is a separate image. The translation merges and misassigns these images.

issues.span: Like ice, they are clear and unobtrusive, yet they are still
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 means 'dissolving/yielding like ice about to melt', not 'clear and unobtrusive, yet still'.

issues.span: Like a primitive state, they are vast and open
issues.advice: 敦兮其若樸 means 'simple/uncarved like raw wood'; 曠兮其若谷 means 'open/vast like a valley'. The two images are conflated and misassigned.

issues.span: Like a valley, they are full and undifferentiated
issues.advice: 渾兮其若濁 means 'mixed/undifferentiated like muddy water', not 'full'; the valley image belongs to 曠兮其若谷.

issues.span: What can make them turbid and still? What can make them clear and calm? What can make them tranquil and enduring?
issues.advice: 孰能濁以靜之徐清 means 'Who can, being turbid, quiet it so it gradually clears?' and 孰能安以乆動之徐生 means 'Who can, being at rest, through long movement gradually bring forth life?' The rhetorical structure and causal 'gradually' sense are lost.

issues.span: they can endure without change
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'thus they can be worn/old without needing to be newly completed' — i.e., they do not seek renewal/completion. 'Endure without change' is inaccurate.

issues.span: the art of being a scholar
issues.advice: 士 in this Daoist context is a practitioner/person of worth, not a scholar; use 'true person/practitioner' terminology.

issues.span: Like a primitive state, they are vast and open. Like a valley, they are full and undifferentiated.
issues.advice: The parallel simile structure (豫若…猶若…儼若…渙若…敦兮…曠兮…渾兮…) should be preserved as a consistent series of 'like…' clauses; current rendering breaks the parallelism and reads awkwardly.

payload.translation: The wise who practiced the Way were subtle, mysterious, profound, and beyond recognition. For it is precisely because they are unrecognizable that they are strengthened and their demeanor is calm and easy. What can make them tranquil and enduring? The one who seeks to preserve this way does not wish to be full. For it is precisely because they are not full that they can endure without change.

issues.span: they are strengthened and their demeanor is calm and easy
issues.advice: The source 故彊為之容 means 'therefore one is forced to describe their appearance'; 彊 is 'forced/compelled', not 'strengthened', and 容 is 'appearance/demeanor', not a separate clause. The translation misparses the clause.

issues.span: they seem to fear their four neighbors
issues.advice: 豫若冬涉川猶若畏四鄰: 豫 (hesitant/cautious) and 猶 (wary) are two separate similes; the translation collapses them and drops the 'hesitant like wading a river in winter' image.

issues.span: like a guest, they are open and transparent
issues.advice: 儼若客 means 'dignified/reverent like a guest'; 儼 is 'dignified', not 'open and transparent'. The rendering inverts the sense.

issues.span: Like ice, they are clear and unobtrusive, yet they are still
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 means 'yielding/dissolving like ice about to melt'; 渙 is 'scattered/dissolving', not 'clear and unobtrusive'.

issues.span: Like a primitive state, they are vast and open
issues.advice: 敦兮其若樸 means 'simple/uncarved like raw wood'; 敦 is 'simple/sincere', 樸 is 'uncarved wood'. 'Primitive state' and 'vast and open' misassign the images (曠兮其若谷 is the valley simile).

issues.span: Like a valley, they are full and undifferentiated
issues.advice: 曠兮其若谷 means 'open/vast like a valley'; 渾兮其若濁 means 'undifferentiated/murky like turbid water'. The translation merges the two and reverses 'open' into 'full'.

issues.span: What can make them turbid and still? What can make them clear and calm? What can make them tranquil and enduring?
issues.advice: 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生 asks 'Who can, being turbid, quiet it to gradually clear? Who can, being at rest, stir it to gradually live?' The translation turns rhetorical questions about self-cultivation into unrelated 'what can make them...' questions and drops 徐 (gradually).

issues.span: they can endure without change
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'thus they can be worn/old without needing new completion' — i.e., they do not seek renewal/newness. 'Endure without change' misses 弊 (worn) and 新成 (newly completed).

issues.span: the Way
issues.advice: 道 in this Daoist classic is conventionally rendered 'the Way' (acceptable), but 士 is 'the scholar/gentleman/person of service', not simply 'the wise'; 善為士者 is 'those skilled in being a true person/scholar'.

issues.span: For it is precisely because they are unrecognizable that they are strengthened and their demeanor is calm and easy.
issues.advice: The clause is grammatically awkward and logically disconnected; restructure to reflect 'therefore one is forced to describe them'.

payload.translation: The virtuous who practiced the Way were subtle, mysterious, profound, and beyond recognition. For it is precisely because they are unrecognizable that they are strengthened, their demeanor calm and easy. Like a person hesitating to wade through a river in winter, they seem to fear their four neighbors; like a guest, they are open and transparent. Like ice, they are yielding and dissolving yet still; like a primitive state, they are vast and open; like a valley, they are undifferentiated and murky. What can make them turbid and still? What can make them clear and calm? What can make them tranquil and enduring? The one who seeks to preserve this Way does not wish to be full. For it is precisely because they are not full that they can endure without change.

issues.span: they are strengthened, their demeanor calm and easy
issues.advice: The source 故彊為之容 means 'therefore one is forced to describe their appearance'; 彊 (qiǎng) means 'forced/reluctantly', not 'strengthened'. The clause is being misread and merged incorrectly.

issues.span: 豫若冬涉川猶若畏四鄰
issues.advice: These are two separate similes: 'hesitant like one crossing a river in winter' and 'cautious like one fearing the four neighbors'. The translation collapses them into one and misassigns 豫/猶.

issues.span: 儼若客渙若冰將釋
issues.advice: 儼若客 means 'dignified/serious like a guest', not 'open and transparent'. 渙若冰將釋 means 'scattered/dissolving like ice about to melt', not 'yielding and dissolving yet still'.

issues.span: 敦兮其若樸曠兮其若谷渾兮其若濁
issues.advice: The three parallel similes are misaligned: 敦兮其若樸 = 'simple/uncarved like raw wood', 曠兮其若谷 = 'vast/open like a valley', 渾兮其若濁 = 'undifferentiated like muddy water'. The translation swaps attributes (e.g., 'primitive state... vast and open' attaches 曠 to 樸).

issues.span: 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生
issues.advice: The rhetorical questions are mistranslated. Meaning: 'Who can, from turbidity, by stillness make it gradually clear? Who can, from stability, by long movement make it gradually live/arise?' The translation renders them as three disconnected questions and loses the 濁→清 and 安→生 progression.

issues.span: 故能弊不新成
issues.advice: 弊不新成 means 'able to be worn/old without needing new completion' — i.e., they can endure decay and do not seek renewal. 'Endure without change' is inaccurate.

issues.span: The virtuous who practiced the Way
issues.advice: 善為士者 is 'those skilled in being a 士 (scholar/officer/master)', not 'the virtuous who practiced the Way'. 士 should be rendered as 'scholar/master/officer'.

issues.span: beyond recognition
issues.advice: 深不可識 means 'so deep as to be unknowable/impenetrable', not 'beyond recognition'. 識 here is 'know/discern'.

issues.span: they are open and transparent. Like ice, they are yielding and dissolving yet still
issues.advice: The similes are garbled and the parallel structure of the original is lost; each 若 clause should map to one distinct image.

payload.translation: Celui qui sait bien faire le sage est subtil, mystérieux, profond et inconnu. C'est parce qu'il est inconnu qu'il est créé avec une grande facilité, une grande sérénité, comme si l'on traversait une rivière en hiver, comme si l'on craignait les quatre voisins, comme si l'on était un étranger, comme si l'eau se dissolvait, comme si l'on se préparait à la fonte de la glace, comme si l'on était un homme brut, comme si l'on était dans une vallée, comme si l'on était dans une masse turbulente. Qui peut rendre la turbidité calme ? Qui peut la faire s'adoucir ? Qui peut la faire s'apaiser ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? C'est celui qui ne veut pas être plein qu'il peut être épuisé, qu'il peut être renouvelé, qu'il peut être créé.

issues.span: Celui qui sait bien faire le sage est subtil
issues.advice: The subject is the ancient master (善為士者), not 'one who knows how to make the sage'; render as 'Ceux qui, dans l'antiquité, excellaient comme maîtres...'.

issues.span: il est créé avec une grande facilité, une grande sérénité
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'one is forced to describe/outline him', not 'he is created with ease/serenity'; the whole clause is mistranslated.

issues.span: comme si l'on craignait les quatre voisins
issues.advice: 畏四鄰 means 'fearing the neighboring states' (cautious, watchful), not 'fearing the four neighbors' literally; adjust to 'comme s'il redoutait ses voisins'.

issues.span: comme si l'eau se dissolvait, comme si l'on se préparait à la fonte de la glace
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 is one image: 'dissolving like ice about to melt'; the translation splits and distorts it.

issues.span: Qui peut rendre la turbidité calme ? Qui peut la faire s'adoucir ? Qui peut la faire s'apaiser ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la f
issues.advice: The source has two rhetorical questions (孰能濁以靜之徐清 / 孰能安以乆動之徐生); the translation invents repeated questions and omits the second (安以乆動之徐生).

issues.span: C'est celui qui ne veut pas être plein qu'il peut être épuisé, qu'il peut être renouvelé, qu'il peut être créé.
issues.advice: 夫惟不盈故能弊不新成 means 'precisely because he does not seek fullness, he can remain worn without needing renewal'; the rendering 'peut être épuisé/renouvelé/créé' inverts and multiplies the sense.

issues.span: brut
issues.advice: 樸 is 'uncarved block / simple, raw (simplicity)', not 'brut' (brutal/raw); use 'comme le bois non taillé' or 'dans sa simplicité'.

issues.span: un étranger
issues.advice: 儼若客 means 'grave/reserved like a guest', not merely 'a foreigner'; use 'comme un invité' with the sense of deference.

issues.span: comme si l'on était dans une masse turbulente
issues.advice: 渾兮其若濁 means 'chaotic/undifferentiated like muddy water'; 'masse turbulente' is unclear and awkward.

issues.span: Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? (repeated five times)
issues.advice: Remove the repeated sentences; they are not in the source and break the text.

issues.span: Celui qui sait bien faire le sage
issues.advice: The Daoist notion of the 士 (master/adept) and the paradoxical style of the Daodejing are lost; render in the register of a classical philosophical text.

payload.translation: Celui qui, dans l'antiquité, excelle comme maître, est subtil, mystérieux, profond et inconnu. C'est parce qu'il est inconnu qu'il est créé avec une grande facilité, une grande sérénité, comme si l'on traversait une rivière en hiver, comme si l'on craignait ses voisins, comme si l'on était un invité, comme si l'eau se dissolvait, comme si l'on se préparait à la fonte de la glace, comme si l'on était un homme non taillé, comme si l'on était dans une vallée, comme si l'on était dans une masse indifférenciée. Qui peut rendre la turbidité calme ? Qui peut la faire s'adoucir ? Qui peut la faire s'apaiser ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? C'est celui qui ne veut pas être plein qu'il peut être épuisé, qu'il peut être renouvelé, qu'il peut être créé.

issues.span: il est créé avec une grande facilité, une grande sérénité
issues.advice: The source 故彊為之容 means 'therefore one is forced to describe his appearance'; the translation invents 'créé avec facilité/sérénité' and misparses 彊為之容.

issues.span: comme si l'on craignait ses voisins
issues.advice: 畏四鄰 means 'fearing the four neighbors' (cautious of surrounding states); 'ses voisins' loses the sense of the four neighboring states.

issues.span: comme si l'eau se dissolvait, comme si l'on se préparait à la fonte de la glace
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 is a single image: 'dissolving like ice about to melt'; the translation splits and duplicates it incorrectly.

issues.span: Qui peut rendre la turbidité calme ? Qui peut la faire s'adoucir ? Qui peut la faire s'apaiser ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la f
issues.advice: The source has two rhetorical questions: 孰能濁以靜之徐清 (who can, being turbid, be stilled and gradually clear?) and 孰能安以乆動之徐生 (who can, being at rest, be stirred and gradually come to life?). The translation repeats a single question many times and omits the second.

issues.span: C'est celui qui ne veut pas être plein qu'il peut être épuisé, qu'il peut être renouvelé, qu'il peut être créé
issues.advice: 保此道者不欲盈夫惟不盈故能弊不新成 means 'one who preserves this Way does not desire fullness; only because he is not full can he be worn without needing renewal'. The translation garbles the syntax and invents 'créé'.

issues.span: comme si l'on était un homme non taillé
issues.advice: 敦兮其若樸: 樸 is 'uncarved wood/block', a key Daoist term; render as 'comme le bois non taillé' rather than 'homme non taillé'.

issues.span: comme si l'on était dans une masse indifférenciée
issues.advice: 渾兮其若濁 means 'chaotic/muddy like turbid water', not 'masse indifférenciée'; keep the turbidity image consistent with 濁 later.

issues.span: comme si l'on traversait une rivière en hiver, comme si l'on craignait ses voisins, comme si l'on était un invité, comme si l'eau se dissolvait
issues.advice: The chain of 'comme si' clauses is repetitive and ungrammatical in places; restructure to reflect the parallel images of the original.

issues.span: il est créé avec une grande facilité, une grande sérénité
issues.advice: The Daoist self-effacement and the notion of 容 (appearance/description) are lost; the passage should convey the master's inscrutability, not creation.

payload.translation: Celui qui excelle dans la voie du Maître est subtil, mystérieux, profond et inconnu. C'est parce qu'il est inconnu qu'on est forcé de le décrire avec une grande facilité et une grande sérénité, comme si l'on traversait une rivière en hiver, comme si l'on craignait ses voisins, comme si l'on était un invité, comme si l'eau se dissolvait, comme si l'on se préparait à la fonte de la glace, comme si l'on était un homme non taillé, comme si l'on était dans une vallée, comme si l'on était dans une masse turbide. Qui peut rendre la turbidité calme ? Qui peut la faire s'adoucir ? Qui peut la faire s'apaiser ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? C'est celui qui ne veut pas être plein qu'il peut être épuisé, qu'il peut être renouvelé.

issues.span: on est forcé de le décrire avec une grande facilité et une grande sérénité
issues.advice: The source 彊為之容 means 'one is forced to describe his appearance/form'; 豫 (yù) begins the next clause meaning 'hesitant/cautious', not 'facilité'. The translation misparses the clause boundary and adds 'sérénité' not in the text.

issues.span: comme si l'eau se dissolvait, comme si l'on se préparait à la fonte de la glace
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 means 'yielding like ice about to melt'—a single image. The translation splits it into two and adds 'l'eau se dissolvait' not present.

issues.span: Qui peut la faire s'adoucir ? Qui peut la faire s'apaiser ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? ... (repeated)
issues.advice: The source 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生 has two rhetorical questions: 'Who can, from turbidity, by stillness make it gradually clear? Who can, from stability, by long movement make it gradually live/arise?' The translation invents multiple repeated questions and omits 徐清/徐生 and 乆動.

issues.span: C'est celui qui ne veut pas être plein qu'il peut être épuisé, qu'il peut être renouvelé
issues.advice: 保此道者不欲盈夫惟不盈故能弊不新成 means 'One who preserves this Way does not desire fullness; only because he is not full can he be worn/old without needing renewal.' The translation garbles the syntax and reverses 不新成.

issues.span: Celui qui excelle dans la voie du Maître
issues.advice: 善為士者 means 'those skilled in being a true scholar/practitioner (士)', not 'la voie du Maître'. 士 is the subject, not 'Maître'.

issues.span: comme si l'on était dans une masse turbide
issues.advice: 渾兮其若濁 means 'chaotic/undifferentiated like muddy water'; 'masse turbide' is unidiomatic and loses the simile structure.

payload.translation: 古に賢なる士は微妙玄通深不可知なり。未知にして強為之容豫、如冬涉川、猶如畏四鄰、儼如客渙、如冰將釋、敦兮其若樸、曠兮其若谷、渾兮其若濁。孰能濁以静之？徐清。孰能安以久動之？徐生。保此道者不欲盈。夫惟不盈故能弊不新成。

issues.span: 未知にして強為之容豫
issues.advice: The source reads 夫惟不可識故彊為之容 (therefore, since it cannot be known, one forcibly describes its appearance); the translation drops 故 and misparses 彊為之容豫, merging 容 with 豫. Render 彊為之容 as '強いて之が容を為す' and keep 豫 as the start of the next clause.

issues.span: 儼如客渙
issues.advice: 儼若客 and 渙若冰將釋 are two separate similes; 渙 belongs with 若冰將釋, not with 客. Split as 儼として客の若く、渙として冰の將に釋けんとするが若し.

issues.span: 孰能濁以静之？徐清。孰能安以久動之？徐生。
issues.advice: The rhetorical questions and answers are mis-segmented; 徐清 and 徐生 are the predicates of the same clauses ('who can, being turbid, quiet it so it gradually clears?'). Render as 孰か能く濁りて以て之を静めて徐かに清からしめん、孰か能く安んじて以て久しく之を動かして徐かに生ぜしめん.

issues.span: 賢なる士
issues.advice: 善為士者 is 'one skilled in being a shi (士)'; 賢なる士 shifts the sense to 'virtuous/worthy scholar'. Use 善く士たる者 or 善く為す士.

issues.span: 古に賢なる士は
issues.advice: 古に is unidiomatic; use 古の善く士たる者は or 古えの….

issues.span: 夫惟不盈故能弊不新成
issues.advice: The final clause is left unparsed and reads as ungrammatical Japanese; it needs a rendering such as 夫れ惟だ盈たざるが故に、能く弊れて新たに成らず.

payload.translation: 古の善く士たる者は微妙玄通深不可知なり。未知にして強いて之が容豫、如冬涉川、猶如畏四鄰、儼として客の若く、渙として氷の将に釋けんとするが若し。敦兮其若樸、曠兮其若谷、渾兮其若濁。孰能濁以静之？徐清。孰能安以久動之？徐生。保此道者不欲盈。夫れ惟だ盈たざるが故に、能く弊れて新たに成らず。

issues.span: 未知にして強いて之が容豫
issues.advice: The source reads 夫惟不可識故彊為之容 (only because it cannot be known, one forcibly describes its appearance). The translation renders 不可識 as 未知 ('not yet known'), losing the sense of 'cannot be known/recognized'; 彊為之容 is also garbled as 之が容豫, merging 容 with the following 豫. Render as 識るべからざるが故に強いて之が容を為す.

issues.span: 徐清
issues.advice: 孰能濁以靜之徐清 means 'who can, being turbid, quiet it and slowly clarify it?' The translation splits into a question 孰能濁以静之？ followed by a bare 徐清, breaking the syntax; the 徐清 should be the result clause of the same sentence.

issues.span: 徐生
issues.advice: Same issue as 徐清: 孰能安以久動之徐生 should keep 徐生 as the result of the same clause, not a detached fragment.

issues.span: 能く弊れて新たに成らず
issues.advice: Source 故能弊不新成 means 'thus can be worn/old without being newly completed' — i.e., able to endure decay rather than being made new. The translation 弊れて新たに成らず is ambiguous and reads as 'is not newly made'; clarify as 故に能く弊れて新たに成らず (able to be worn out and not newly completed), ensuring 能 modifies 弊.

issues.span: 容豫、如冬涉川
issues.advice: The punctuation and phrasing 容豫、如冬涉川 is ungrammatical; 豫 begins the next simile (豫兮若冬涉川). Separate as 強いて之が容を為す。豫として冬の川を涉るが若く.

issues.span: 士
issues.advice: In this Daoist context 士 refers to the adept/master; 士 alone in Japanese may read as 'samurai/gentleman'. Consider 士（道を修める者） or 善く士たる者 to disambiguate.

payload.translation: 古の善く士たる者は微妙玄通深不可識なり。未知にして強いて之が識るべからざるが故に、強いて之が容を為す。豫として冬の川を涉るが若く、猶如畏四鄰、儼として客の若く、渙として氷の将に釋けんとするが若し。敦兮其若樸、曠兮其若谷、渾兮其若濁。孰能濁以静之？徐清。孰能安以久動之？徐生。保此道者不欲盈。夫れ惟だ不盈故に、能く弊れて新たに成らず。

issues.span: 未知にして強いて之が識るべからざるが故に
issues.advice: The source reads 夫惟不可識 (only because it cannot be known), not 未知 (not yet known). The rendering adds a temporal sense 'not yet known' that is absent; should convey 'only because it cannot be known'.

issues.span: 猶如畏四鄰
issues.advice: This is left as an unassimilated Chinese fragment (猶如畏四鄰) inside a Japanese sentence; it should be rendered in Japanese, e.g. 猶お四鄰を畏るるが如く, to match the parallel 若く constructions.

issues.span: 能く弊れて新たに成らず
issues.advice: The source 能弊不新成 means 'can be worn/old without being newly completed' — i.e., able to remain worn rather than made new. The translation '弊れて新たに成らず' is ambiguous and can read as 'does not newly become'; clarify the sense of 不新成 (not being made anew / not requiring renewal).

issues.span: 強いて之が識るべからざるが故に、強いて之が容を為す
issues.advice: The double 強いて and the awkward 之が識るべからざる construction are hard to parse; the first clause should express 'since it cannot be known' and the second 'therefore one forcibly describes its appearance', avoiding repetition and the ungrammatical 識るべからざる.

issues.span: 孰能濁以静之？徐清。孰能安以久動之？徐生。
issues.advice: The rhetorical questions are split from their answers with periods, breaking the 孰能…徐… parallel structure; the 徐清/徐生 should be joined as the predicate answering each question (e.g. …静めて徐に清らかにする).

issues.span: 豫として冬の川を涉るが若く
issues.advice: 豫 (hesitant/cautious) is rendered with the Sino-Japanese 豫 as a bare adverb; better to use a Japanese equivalent such as ためらうさま/慎重に to convey the Daoist term's sense rather than a transliterated character.

payload.translation: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has already been going on for more than two years. Yet, while I am in the process of writing it, I am constantly recalling it. This shows that I am not a man of "establishing words." For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man, so that men write to immortalize others, and others write to immortalize men. Ultimately, it is unclear who is immortalizing whom, until it finally resolves to immortalizing Ah Q, as if there is a ghost in my thoughts.

issues.span: it has already been going on for more than two years
issues.advice: The source says '已经不止一两年了' — 'more than a year or two' / 'not just one or two years,' not 'more than two years.' The translation narrows the meaning incorrectly.

issues.span: I am constantly recalling it
issues.advice: '往回想' means 'thinking back / having second thoughts / hesitating,' not 'recalling it.' The sense is that while wanting to write, the narrator keeps drawing back or reconsidering.

issues.span: men write to immortalize others, and others write to immortalize men
issues.advice: The source '人以文传，文以人传' means 'the man is transmitted/immortalized through the writing, and the writing is transmitted through the man' — i.e., person relies on text and text relies on person. The translation reverses and garbles this reciprocal relationship.

issues.span: a man of "establishing words"
issues.advice: '立言' is a classical Confucian concept (one of the 'three immortalities': 立德, 立功, 立言). A literal gloss 'establishing words' is opaque; consider rendering as 'a man who establishes words (li yan)' or 'one who achieves immortality through words,' preserving the allusion.

issues.span: as if there is a ghost in my thoughts
issues.advice: '仿佛思想里有鬼似的' is closer to 'as if a ghost were in my mind' — acceptable, but 'thoughts' slightly shifts; minor.

This shows that I am not a man of "establishing words." For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man, so that men write to immortalize others, and others write to immortalize men. issues.span: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has already been going on for more than a year or two
issues.advice: The source says '我要给阿Q做正传，已经不止一两年了' — the intent is that the author has been *intending/planning* to write the biography for more than a year or two, not that the writing has been ongoing. Render as 'I have wanted to write a proper biography of Ah Q for more than a year or two now.'

issues.span: while I am in the process of writing it, I am constantly thinking back to it
issues.advice: '一面要做，一面又往回想' means 'while wanting to write it, I keep having second thoughts / keep turning it over in my mind' — not 'thinking back to it.' Convey the hesitation/reconsideration.

issues.span: a biography
issues.advice: '正传' is a specific term (a 'proper/orthodox biography,' echoing the classical 正传 genre). 'A biography' loses this; consider 'a proper biography' or 'an orthodox biography.'

issues.span: men write to immortalize others, and others write to immortalize men
issues.advice: '人以文传，文以人传' means 'the man is transmitted/immortalized through his writing, and the writing through the man' — i.e., persons are handed down via their works and works via their persons. The current rendering reverses and garbles this; render as 'the man is handed down through the writing, and the writing through the man.'

issues.span: until it finally resolves to immortalizing Ah Q
issues.advice: '而终于归结到传阿Q' means 'and in the end it all comes down to writing the biography of Ah Q.' 'Resolves to immortalizing' is awkward and shifts meaning; use 'comes down to writing Ah Q's biography.'

issues.span: as if there is a ghost in my mind
issues.advice: '仿佛思想里有鬼似的' is closer to 'as if a ghost were at work in my thoughts' — acceptable but 'in my mind' slightly flattens; consider 'as if there were a ghost in my thoughts.'

payload.translation: I have wanted to write a proper biography of Ah Q for more than a year or two now. Yet, while I am in the process of writing it, I constantly turn it over in my mind. This shows that I am not a man of "establishing words." For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man, so that the man is handed down through the writing, and the writing through the man. Ultimately, it comes down to writing Ah Q's biography, as if there were a ghost in my thoughts.

issues.span: a man of "establishing words"
issues.advice: 『立言』 is a Confucian concept (from the 'three immortalities': 立德, 立功, 立言). A literal gloss 'establishing words' is opaque to English readers; consider rendering the sense, e.g. 'one who establishes his name through words/writing' or 'a man who leaves behind words that endure'.

issues.span: Ultimately, it comes down to writing Ah Q's biography
issues.advice: The source '而终于归结到传阿Q' is the conclusion of the preceding reasoning about who transmits whom; the translation drops the connective logic ('and finally it all comes down to...'), making the leap abrupt. Add the connective to preserve the argumentative flow.

issues.span: while I am in the process of writing it, I constantly turn it over in my mind
issues.advice: '一面要做，一面又往回想' means 'while wanting to do it, I keep turning back/reconsidering' — the tension is between the urge to write and the hesitation. 'In the process of writing it' shifts the meaning to being mid-writing; render as 'even as I want to do it, I keep holding back/reconsidering'.

payload.translation: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat obscure; even his former deeds are vague. For the people of Wuzhuang, as long as he helps them, they treat him as a joke, and never pay attention to his deeds. Aq himself does not say so, but when he argues with others, he occasionally squints his eyes and says: "We were once much more prosperous than you! What are you?"

issues.span: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat obscure
issues.advice: The opening is ungrammatical and misrenders the structure; render as 'Not only are Ah Q's name and place of origin somewhat obscure' to preserve the 'not only...even' construction.

issues.span: Aq
issues.advice: The standard rendering of 阿Q is 'Ah Q' (Lu Xun's canonical English name), not 'Aq'.

issues.span: Wuzhuang
issues.advice: 未庄 is conventionally rendered 'Weizhuang' (or left as 'Wei Village'); 'Wuzhuang' is a nonstandard romanization.

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they treat him as a joke
issues.advice: The source means they only ever want him to help and only make fun of him; 'as long as' introduces a false conditional. Render as 'they only wanted him to help and only made fun of him'.

issues.span: Aq himself does not say so
issues.advice: 『而阿Q自己也不说』 means Ah Q himself did not talk about it (his 行状/deeds), not 'does not say so'; render as 'Nor did Ah Q himself speak of it'.

issues.span: squints his eyes
issues.advice: 瞪着眼睛 means 'glare' or 'stare wide-eyed', not 'squint'; render as 'glaring'.

issues.span: We were once much more prosperous than you
issues.advice: 『我们先前——比你阔的多啦』 uses 阔 (rich/great); 'prosperous' is acceptable but 'much richer/greater than you' is closer; the dash pause should be preserved.

issues.span: What are you?
issues.advice: 『你算是什么东西！』 is an insult meaning 'What do you amount to?' / 'Who do you think you are?'; 'What are you?' is too literal and weak.

payload.translation: Not only are Ah Q's name and place of origin somewhat obscure, but even his former deeds are vague. For the people of Weizhuang, as long as he helps them, they only want him to help and only make fun of him; they never pay attention to his deeds. Nor did Ah Q himself speak of it, but when he argued with others, he occasionally glared and said, "We were once much richer than you! What are you?"

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they only want him to help and only make fun of him
issues.advice: The clause is redundant and awkward; render the two parallel verbs (帮忙/玩笑) more concisely, e.g. 'they only wanted his help and made fun of him'.

issues.span: Nor did Ah Q himself speak of it
issues.advice: 'it' has no clear antecedent; the source refers to his 行状 (deeds/record), so use 'them' or 'his deeds'.

issues.span: We were once much richer than you!
issues.advice: The 我们先前 is a boastful 'we (my family/we) were once far better off than you'; 'much richer' is acceptable but 'far better off' better captures 阔 in this ironic context.

payload.translation: Ah Q's name and place of origin are obscure, and even his past deeds are vague. For the people of Weizhuang, as long as he helps them, they only want his help and make fun of him; they never pay attention to his deeds. Nor did Ah Q himself speak of it, but when he argued with others, he occasionally glared and said, "We were once much better off than you! What are you?"

issues.span: they only want his help and make fun of him
issues.advice: The source '只要他帮忙，只拿他玩笑' means they merely use him for help and for amusement; the rendering adds 'want his help' redundantly and slightly shifts the sense. Consider 'they only had him help them and made fun of him'.

issues.span: Nor did Ah Q himself speak of it
issues.advice: '也不说' refers to not speaking about his 行状/past deeds; 'it' is acceptable but could be clearer as 'his past'.

issues.span: We were once much better off than you!
issues.advice: '阔' here echoes the earlier '阔的多啦' and carries the sense of wealth/status; 'better off' is acceptable but 'much richer than you' is closer to the original.

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they only want his help and make fun of him
issues.advice: The clause is awkward and repetitive; restructure for smoother flow.
